title: Choux buns with Swiss cream
subtitle: Hollow choux buns filled with pastry cream and whipped cream
verified_note: Not made by the maker himself yet. The amounts follow from the base recipes; the filling step has not been tested.

time.note: About 2.5 hours from empty worktop to filled choux buns, most of it waiting and baking.

context: This is the same dough as in the separate choux recipe, the same buns, and the same cream as on the two base pages — no second version that can drift apart. Change something in the dough and it changes here too. The only step of its own is the filling, and that is mostly a matter of timing: a bun filled too early goes soft, and so does one left standing too long.

spuitzak met kartelmondje 8-10 mm.name: piping bag with an 8-10 mm star nozzle
spuitzak met kartelmondje 8-10 mm.note: Or a sharp knife and a teaspoon.

stap-1.title: Get the buns ready
stap-1.text: Let the buns cool completely on a rack. Prick a hole in the base with a small knife or the tip of the nozzle, or cut them in half horizontally.
stap-1.why: Filling from the bottom keeps the top intact and gives an even filling. Cutting in half is quicker and easier to fill, but the wall goes soft sooner.
tips: Only fill when they are really cold; warm buns draw moisture and turn leathery.

stap-2.title: Filling
stap-2.text: Put the Swiss cream in a piping bag with a star nozzle and fill each bun from below until you feel resistance and no more cream goes in. Or spoon the cream into the cut buns.
stap-2.why: Until you feel resistance: a half-filled bun tastes of air. Push too far and the wall bursts.
tips: About 15 g per bun; for 50 buns that is exactly 750 g of cream.

stap-3.title: Serving
stap-3.text: Dust with icing sugar and serve within two hours. Keep them in the fridge until then and take them out 15-30 minutes before serving.
stap-3.why: The cream is cold and the wall takes up moisture. Filled for longer than a day, the buns go soft and lose their bite.
tips: Unfilled buns keep for a week airtight; fill them on the day itself.

0.q: How much cream goes into one bun?
0.a: About 15 grams. For 50 buns that is 750 grams of Swiss cream.

1.q: Can I fill the buns in advance?
1.a: Better not. Filled they keep for a day in the fridge, but the wall goes soft. Bake and fill on the day you eat them, or keep the parts separate.

0.oorzaak: filled too early or kept too long
0.fix: fill when cold, serve within two hours

1.oorzaak: pushed too hard, or the wall is too thin
1.fix: pipe gently until resistance, and bake the buns golden brown and properly dried
